terms.gloss: sharing in, taking part in; as a noun, a sharer, a participant
terms.grammar: adjective and noun, third declension, one ending; + genitive
evidence: Cic. Att. 2.25.2: aut expediēs nōs omnī molestiā aut eris particeps
Ter. Heaut. 428: cujus maximē tē fierī participem cupis
terms.comment: The one who shares or takes part in something, with the genitive of what is shared: particeps cōnsiliōrum, sollicitūdinis, nūntiī. Near it stand socius, a partner or ally, and cōnsors, one who shares a lot or an inheritance (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: one who is present at or takes part in (+ dat.)
terms.comment: For the people present at an event, a meeting or a game: quī convīviō, lūdīs, cōnsiliō intersunt, those taking part in the dinner, the games, the meeting.

phrases.latin: quā rē advolā; aut expediēs nōs omnī molestiā aut eris particeps
phrases.english: so fly here: either you will get me out of all this trouble or you will share it

phrases.latin: Menedēme, salvē: nūntium apportō tibi cujus maximē tē fierī participem cupis.
phrases.english: Good day, Menedemus: I bring you news you will be very glad to share in.

phrases.latin: cūr ego absum vel spectātor laudum tuārum vel particeps vel socius vel minister cōnsiliōrum?
phrases.english: why am I away, unable to watch your successes, or to share in your plans, as partner or as helper?

sources: Lewis & Short: particeps · Lewis & Short: intersum
